children: U.S. President Donald Trump and his wealth managers executed nearly 28.7K security transactions in the 17 months following his second inauguration—outpacing all members of Congress combined—even as he pushes legislation banning lawmakers from buying stocks, according to a media report Tuesday.
During that same period, Capitol Hill lawmakers collectively reported about 22.2K similar transactions, Bloomberg reported, citing security transaction disclosure forms.

The contrast marks a notable shift from his first term, when Trump's financial disclosures contained mostly illiquid real estate holdings and other privately held ventures. His portfolio now spans thousands of holdings in stocks

passed by House Republicans in July exclusively restricts members of Congress, their spouses and dependent children. The legislation leaves the presidency untouched—even though the commander-in-chief has singularly wide-ranging access to U.S. intelligence and the power to influence entire sectors with an executive order or social media post.

Backing the proposed House measure, Trump had stated in his recent State of the Union address that it must be enacted "without delay" so that members of Congress "cannot corruptly profit from using insider information." He remains the only U.S. president this century to disclose active trading of individual stocks, continuing transactions that would be prohibited for lawmakers under the very legislation he champions.
